embedding.label: Java OOP intro chunks
embedding.subject: JAVA_OOP
embedding.content:
## Objects and classes
A class defines fields and methods. Each object keeps its own state. Constructors initialize a new object.

## Arrays
An array stores values in ordered positions. Index starts at 0 and loops are commonly used to read every element.

embedding.label: DSA Java - array list basics
embedding.subject: DSA_JAVA
embedding.content:
## Dynamic arrays
An array list supports random access by index. Insertions at the end are efficient, while insertions in the middle may require shifting later elements.

chunks.contentText: A class defines the structure and behavior of objects. Encapsulation means bundling state and methods together and restricting direct access where appropriate.
An array stores multiple values of the same type. The first element is at index 0 and loops are commonly used to traverse the array.
A for loop repeats a block of code for a known number of iterations. Arrays in C use zero-based indexing and store values in contiguous memory.
